title: Readability and responsive typography
learningObjectives: Explain readability and responsive typography and use it in a practical layout.

understand.concept: Readable typography depends on font size, line length, line height, contrast, spacing, and responsive behaviour. clamp() creates a fluid value with minimum and maximum limits. A comfortable line length often uses a max-width measured in ch.
understand.whyItMatters: Test at narrow and wide viewports, with browser text scaling, and with the scripts used by learners. A size that works in English may have different visual density in another writing system.
understand.analogy: A comfortable reading layout has a useful line length and enough space between lines. The best values depend on content and readers.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy supports intuition; browser layout follows the CSS formatting and sizing rules.

explain.narrative: The heading and paragraph scale with viewport width while staying within their defined limits.

practise.guidedTask: Build a reading card with a maximum line length, fluid heading size, and comfortable line-height. Test phone and desktop widths.
practise.independentTask: Create a small responsive component that demonstrates this concept. Test it at a narrow viewport and inspect its computed styles.

questions.answer: A value bounded by a minimum and a maximum
